identificationModule.briefTitle: Development of Ivermectin for Alcohol Use Disorders
identificationModule.officialTitle: Repositioning Ivermectin for the Treatment of Alcohol Use Disorders

descriptionModule.briefSummary: Current pharmacotherapies for alcohol use disorders (AUDs) have limited efficacy. Thus, the development of effective treatments for AUDs represents an important public health objective. Repositioning, i.e. using existing approved drugs for other indications, represents a fast and economically feasible approach for drug development. Ivermectin (IVM) is an FDA-approved antiparasitic medication that can significantly reduce alcohol intake in mice, suggesting that it may be useful in the treatment of AUDs in humans. The goal of this project is to provide key clinical evidence that IVM can be repositioned as a novel therapeutic agent to treat AUDs.
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: Current pharmacotherapies for alcohol use disorders (AUDs) have limited efficacy. Thus, the development of effective treatments for AUDs represents an important public health objective. Repositioning, i.e. using existing approved drugs for other indications, represents a fast and economically feasible approach for drug development. Ivermectin (IVM) is an FDA-approved antiparasitic medication that can significantly reduce alcohol intake in mice, suggesting that it may be useful in the treatment of AUDs in humans. The goal of this project is to provide key clinical evidence that IVM can be repositioned as a novel therapeutic agent to treat AUDs. We will enroll 10 alcohol dependent individuals in a placebo-controlled randomized pilot safety trial of IVM (30 mg orally once) over a 2-day (1-night) inpatient stay at the UCLA CTRC and employ a well-characterized battery of behavioral paradigms (i.e., alcohol administration and cue exposure). The goals of the study are to test: (a) the safety of combining IVM, at a dose currently shown to be safe in humans (30 mg), with moderate doses of alcohol (0.08 g/dl); and (b) whether IVM reduces the reinforcing effects of alcohol during alcohol administration and whether it reduces alcohol craving during cue exposure, as compared to placebo.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Subjective Effects of Alcohol Using the Alcohol Urge Questionnaire (AUQ)
primaryOutcomes.description: Subjective effects of alcohol will be measured using the Alcohol Urge Questionnaire (AUQ), which consists of 8 items associated with urge to drink alcohol, rated on a 7 point scale (1 = strongly disagree, 7 = strongly agree).
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: During alcohol infusion at BrAC = 0.00, 0.02, 0.04, 0.06, 0.08 g/dl period; which is expected to last approximately 6 hours.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Subjective Effects of Alcohol Using the Drug Effects Questionnaire (DEQ) - "Feel" Subscale
primaryOutcomes.description: Subjective effects of alcohol will be measured using the Drug Effects Questionnaire, which consists of 4 items that capture subjective effects, (feeling effects, liking effects, wanting more and being high). The question "Do you feel any drug effects?" was rated on an 11 point scale from 0 to 10 (higher values represent more effects).
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: During alcohol infusion at BrAC = 0.00, 0.02, 0.04, 0.06, 0.08 g/dl period; which is expected to last approximately 6 hours.

The total score for the Stimulant Subscale ranges from 0 to 70. Mean scores across all subjects are reported below.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Cue-induced Craving Using the Alcohol Urge Questionnaire (AUQ)
primaryOutcomes.description: Cue-induced craving will be measured using the Alcohol Urge Questionnaire (AUQ), which consists of 8 items associated with urge to drink alcohol, rated on a 7 point scale (0 = strongly disagree, 6 = strongly agree). Item scores were averaged and the total score also ranges from 0-6.

Adverse effects will be monitored to determine the safe of combining IVM (30 mg) with moderate doses of alcohol (0.08 g/dl) using the Systematic Assessment for Treatment Emergent Effects (SAFTEE). The SAFTEE is a 24-item checklist in which the participant can identify whether a symptom is present (yes/no), its severity (mild, moderate, severe) and whether it was caused by the medication (yes/no). Data below represents a count of individual adverse effects reported on the SAFTEE during the alcohol infusion.
